security_audit.summary: Static command and network detections are mostly Markdown documentation false positives; the file contains no executable Ruby backtick code or autonomous outbound requests. The main confirmed risk is unsafe secret-handling guidance that can expose API keys through Expo client config and command history. No prompt injection language was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: API secrets are shown as client Expo config values.
remediation.suggestion: Move private API keys to a backend or use EAS secrets only for build-time server-side configuration. Clearly label public client values.

remediation.issue: Secret values are shown directly on the command line.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer interactive secret entry or secure input methods. Warn that command history and process listings can expose command values.

remediation.issue: Deployment commands can publish builds or OTA updates.
remediation.suggestion: Add confirmation guidance before submit, update, credential reset, or production build commands.

semantic_findings.title: Unsafe API Secret Exposure Guidance
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells users to create an API_KEY secret, place process.env.API_KEY in Expo extra config, and read it from app code. Private secrets in client-visible Expo config can be extracted from mobile builds, and direct command values can expose secrets through shell history.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The guidance directly connects an API_KEY secret to Expo client config and app code. This is unsafe for private keys, although public values would be acceptable.

content.user_title: Deploy Expo iOS Apps with EAS
content.value_statement: iOS release work for Expo apps requires EAS profiles, credentials, TestFlight steps, and version rules. This skill gives focused checklists and commands for build, submit, OTA updates, and troubleshooting.
actual_capabilities: Shows initial EAS CLI setup commands for Expo iOS projects.
Provides example EAS build and submit profiles.
Explains development, preview, production, and local iOS build flows.
Lists TestFlight, App Store Connect, and App Store submission steps.
Documents OTA update channels, version increments, and common EAS troubleshooting commands.
limitations: Focuses on iOS workflows and does not cover Android release setup.
Provides static guidance and does not verify Apple or Expo account state.
Uses example identifiers, URLs, and secrets that must be replaced before use.
Does not replace Expo, Apple, or App Store policy documentation.

use_cases.title: Create a First iOS Build
use_cases.description: Set up EAS for an Expo app and choose the right build profile.

use_cases.title: Prepare TestFlight Delivery
use_cases.description: Review App Store Connect fields, credentials, build numbers, and submit steps before tester release.

use_cases.title: Resolve Build and Update Issues
use_cases.description: Use targeted checks for signing errors, stuck processing, crashes, and OTA update delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Set Up iOS Builds
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a new Expo project.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me configure EAS Build for my Expo iOS app. Include the needed project files, profiles, and first build checks.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare TestFlight Submission
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a TestFlight submission plan for my Expo app. Cover credentials, build number, App Store Connect fields, and review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Troubleshoot Build Failure
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused debugging for a failed build.
prompt_templates.prompt: My Expo iOS build failed during signing. Walk me through likely causes, credential checks, and safe recovery steps.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Release Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Expo iOS release workflow. Identify gaps in build profiles, OTA channels, versioning, credentials, and App Store submission readiness.

output_examples.input: Prepare my Expo app for TestFlight.
output: Review bundle identifier, version, build number, and Apple team settings.
Confirm credentials are ready in EAS or local files.
Create a production build and submit it to TestFlight after confirmation.

output_examples.input: My OTA update is not appearing.
output: Check that the build channel matches the update branch.
Confirm the app is not running in development mode.
Restart the app after the update is available.

output_examples.output: The skill returns a release checklist covering screenshots, privacy policy, age rating, export compliance, build selection, and review steps.

best_practices: Confirm the target EAS profile before every build or submission.
Keep private keys on a backend and expose only public client configuration.
Increase iOS build numbers for every App Store upload.
anti_patterns: Do not paste private API keys into client-visible Expo config.
Do not reset signing credentials without confirming team ownership and impact.
Do not publish OTA updates to production without matching the release channel.

faq.question: Does this skill support Android releases?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on Expo iOS builds, TestFlight, App Store submission, and iOS troubleshooting.

faq.question: Can it create Apple Developer accounts?
faq.answer: No. It explains where account, team, and App Store Connect information fits into the workflow.

faq.question: Does it run builds automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides commands and checklists that an agent or user can apply with confirmation.

faq.question: Can it manage certificates?
faq.answer: It explains EAS credential options and manual credential concepts. It does not verify private certificate files.

faq.question: Does it cover OTA updates?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents update branches, channels, common publish steps, and troubleshooting checks.

faq.question: Is it safe for private API keys?
faq.answer: Use caution. Private keys should stay on a backend and should not be exposed in client app config.
